# Draft:Syed Sanwar Ali

(1956-1971)
(1971-2015)
| party = Bangladesh Nationalist Party
Bangladesh Nationalist Freedom Fighter Party
}}
Freedom Fighter Syed Sanwar Ali (known as Sanu; c. (1956 – November 2015) was a freedom fighter and politician. He was the former member secretary of the Chittagong Metropolitan Muktijoddha Unit Command and the president of the local Shatadal Club.
Family Background
The father of the brave freedom fighter Syed Sanwar Ali Sanu, Syed Rashed Ali, a native of Jamal Khan Lane, was a graduate of Calcutta Aligarh University. During the British rule, he passed the Bengal Civil Service Examination with distinction and joined the East Bengal Railway as the Chief Accountant. Later, he served as a board member of the East Bengal Railway. The late Syed Rashed Ali was a selfless philanthropist and a non-publicist social worker. He served as the president of the Jamal Khan Lane Janakalyan Samiti for 16 years from 1955 to 1970. During his tenure, he carried out extensive development activities in the entire Jamal Khan ward. He was one of the founders of the Dost Colony Jame Masjid across Askar Dighi. Social worker Syed Sanwar Ali acquired the universal spirit of a social worker, patriotism, and the great ideals of humanity from his family environment.
Education
Syed Sanwar Ali (Sanu) completed his secondary education from Police Line High School, his higher secondary education from Government City College, Chittagong, and his graduation in Islamic history from Chittagong University.
Participation in Liberation War
Syed Sanwar Ali (Sanu), a freedom fighter who was a student and was only 16 years old, joined the great liberation war after completing his SSC examination in 1971. On the dark night of March 25, when the Pakistani armed forces attacked the peaceful Bengalis, Syed Sanwar Ali (Sanu), Iqbal, Manik, Tunu, Jhantu, Kanchan, Ekram, Shafi, Nuruddin Khaled Babu and Mansur Munna, among others, gathered at the Shatdal Club ground near Askardighi and took an oath to work for the liberation war. After the war started, when they heard about the presence of the Pakistani occupying forces in the DC hills of Chittagong, they collected some weapons through various means. As the banks of Askardighi were close to DC Hills, some freedom fighters from outside took up positions in their area, and they joined forces with them and attacked DC Hills. Many of them were seriously injured. Freedom fighters Manik and Kanchan in particular were shot by Pakistanis, and Manik later died while undergoing treatment. Manik's death created more anger among them towards the Pakistani military. Later, Syed Sanwar Ali (Sanu) along with his friend, freedom fighter Mansur Munna, joined Sector No. 1 under the leadership of Major Ziaur Rahman (Bir Uttam) and Major Rafiqul Islam (Bir Uttam). At such a young age, the strong freedom fighter Syed Sanwar Ali Sanu's immense bravery in taking a firm oath to free the motherland from the invaders surprised even the sector commanders Major Ziaur Rahman and Major Rafiqul Islam. From there, Syed Sanwar Ali (Sanu) and Mansur Munna went to Nazirhat for training and received combat training at Harina Camp, a subdivision 8 km from Sabroom in South Tripura, Tripura state, India. The training camp began on 14 May 1971. Major Ziaur Rahman was the military instructor, MA Hannan was the civilian officer, and Engineer Mosharraf Hossain was the coordinator. After the training, they returned to Nazirhat and directly participated in the liberation war.
Political Affiliations
The brave freedom fighter Syed Sanwar Ali Martyred President Ziaur Rahman believed in Bangladeshi nationalism. In his political life, he served as the vice-president of the Chittagong Kotwali Thana Bangladesh Nationalist Party. He served as the president of the Jamalkhan Ward Bangladesh Nationalist Party adjacent to the Chittagong Metropolitan Bangladesh Nationalist Party office until his death. He also served as the general secretary of the Chittagong Metropolitan Bangladesh Nationalist Party affiliate organization Bangladesh Nationalist Freedom Fighters until his death. In his political life, he led various affiliate organizations of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party at various levels.
Social and Sports Involvement
Former President – Shatdal Club, Askardighir Par, Chittagong.
Former Commander – Freedom Fighter Command Council, Chittagong Metropolitan City.
Former Convener – Discipline Sub-Committee, Muktijuddhar Bijoy Mela Parishad, Chittagong.
Former President – Muktijuddhar Pragati Bahumukhi Samabhai Samity, Khulshi.
Former Acting Chairman - Jamalkhan Lane Social Security Council, Askardighir South Parstha Area, Chittagong.
Former President – Anandbagh Residential Society, Old Biman Office.
Former Councillor (C.J.K.S) – Muktijoddha Krira Chakra.
One of the founders – Hafez Mohammad Sadeq Waqf Estate Jame Masjid, Old Biman Office Lane, Chittagong.
One of the founders - Muktijoddha Pragati Bahumukhi Samabay Samity Jame Masjid, Khulshi.
One of the entrepreneurs – Dost Colony Jame Masjid Modernization Project (Implemented), Askardighi side.
One of the entrepreneurs – Old Biman Office Lane Widening and Sewer Construction Project. (Implemented)
One of the entrepreneurs – Lane Widening Project Adjacent to Dost Colony Mosque and Kacha Bazar, Askardighi side. (Implemented)
One of the entrepreneurs – Lane Widening and Sewer Construction Project Adjacent to Shatdal Club, Askardighi side. (Implemented)
Children
His three children are Syed Omar Ali, Syed Safwan Ali, Syed Sohan Ali
Death
He died of cardiac arrest at the capital's Apollo Hospital on 10 November 2015 at the age of 59. Following his death, various social and political circles in Chittagong expressed their condolences.
Honors
After his death, in his memory, the Chittagong City Corporation proposed to name the road from the old Biman Office (adjacent to the Bangladesh Nationalist Party Chittagong Metropolitan Office) to the Shatadal Club as Bir Muktijoddha Syed Sanwar Ali Sanu Road. The Local Government Department of the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh approved it and the Local Government Department issued a circular instructing the appropriate authority to name the road.
